It sounds like you're carrying a lot of frustration and self-blame, and I want to gently challenge the idea that you're "lazy." Often, what looks like procrastination is actually anxiety, perfectionism, or burnout in disguise—especially for high-achieving students who suddenly struggle. The fact that you care so much about your grades suggests this isn't about not caring; something deeper may be making it hard to start.

Consider trying a few small shifts: break tasks into tiny, almost ridiculously small steps (just open the document, just write one sentence), and try working for only five minutes to lower the barrier to starting. Sometimes removing the pressure to "do it well" and just focusing on "doing something" helps break the cycle. It might also be worth talking to a school counselor or academic support service—they see this pattern frequently and can help you figure out what's really getting in your way. You're clearly capable, and struggling right now doesn't erase that capability.
